newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope, at summit, says rich-poor gap intolerable.
newsitem.headline: Pope, at summit, says rich-poor gap intolerable.

text.p: Pope John Paul called on world leaders on Wednesday to bridge the gulf between rich and poor, telling a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit it was "intolerable" that some people lived in opulence while others starved.

"We have to search together for solutions so that there are no longer hungry people living side by side with people living in opulence," he told heads of state and delegates at the opening of the summit, called to reduce hunger in the world.
"This contrast between poverty and wealth is intolerable for humanity," he said.

The 76-year-old Pope also took a swipe at those who say population control is the key to food security. "Demography alone does not explain the inadequate distribution of food resources. We must put aside the sophist view that when there are many, one is condemned to be poor," the Pope said.
He said the real reasons behind food insecurity often were political instability, wars, and developing countries mired in debt.

The Pope also said food insecurity was sometimes caused by "embargoes imposed without sufficient reasoning". The Vatican has in the past criticised embargoes imposed on Cuba and Iraq, saying they hurt the poor most.
